summary: End-to-end verification of TipJar auth (A) username + optional email, and (B) Forebet auto-post on Rate Wall. All 8 backend regression tests PASS and every frontend flow succeeds. Fresh browser (SW/caches cleared) → header 'Sign up' opens auth modal → username+password only (email blank) creates an account, returns a token and shows the exact welcome toast 'Welcome! Your account is ready 🎉' (NO inbox/verify message). username+password+valid-email signup shows 'Account created! Check your inbox to verify your email 📧'. Login mode hides the email field; login by username AND by email both work (toast '👋 <username>'). Backend also confirmed: /api/auth/register with no email returns user with email_verified=true and multiple null-email accounts can coexist (partial unique index). Tips window (view-tips-btn → [data-testid=tips-window]) renders the Forebet auto-pick tip-card-forebet-2460219 authored by TipJarHQ with league 'Forebet Pick' and market 'Lonestar gewinnt', source='forebet'.

critical_code_review_comments: AuthModal only calls setLang after a successful signup (line 37) but not after a successful login when the returned user has a different language than the current i18n state — the login branch handles this (line 33), so this is fine. No issue.

auth.jsx only persists tj_token in localStorage; the user profile is refetched via GET /api/auth/me on refresh. This is a good pattern (single source of truth), just noting so future testers don't check localStorage for tj_user (there isn't one).

Small UX polish: after an email-less signup the modal shows a fleeting 'Welcome' toast; consider also nudging the user to add an email later in settings so they can recover the account. Not a blocker.

Forebet market strings (e.g. 'Lonestar gewinnt') are German-only regardless of the UI language. If the user is in en/el, this reads a bit off. Consider localising the auto-generated market label. Non-blocking.

rca of the issue: No functional issue found. Two testing-side gotchas worth documenting: (1) force=True on the header signup button caused clicks to be swallowed (the header uses overflow-hidden pill styling); switching to a normal click resolved it. (2) The app does not store the user object under localStorage.tj_user — an early assertion that read 'tj_user' produced a false negative. Verification should rely on tj_token presence + the visible welcome toast.
